title: Ohannes Pasha appointed last Christian mutasarrif of Mount Lebanon
why: Firman amended the Organic Statute (wider council elections, three new ports). He was the last Christian governor before wartime direct rule.

title: Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate population about 414,700
why: Baseline for famine losses: Wikipedia lists 399,530 (1895), 414,747 (1913) and about 200,000 (1918).

title: Silk is 32.9% and diaspora remittances 45.6% of Mount Lebanon income
why: Both income streams were cut by war and blockade; the dependency set up the famine (one source's figures).

title: Ottoman general mobilisation of young males, secret pact with Germany
why: Prelude to war: conscription of Beirut and Mount Lebanon men began before the Ottoman entry into the war.

title: Beirut crowds storm municipality over wheat and flour shortage
why: First war-related grain shortage in Lebanon, two weeks after the Ottoman entry; bakeries looted as rail cars from Aleppo failed to arrive.

title: Beirut mayor Beyhum travels to Aleppo to secure grain wagons
why: He negotiated with the Fourth Army and paid from the municipal treasury; wheat reached Beirut on 19 November 1914.

title: Jamal Pasha appointed governor-general of Syria and Fourth Army commander
why: One Turkish thesis chronology gives this date; he held civil and military powers over Syria, Lebanon and Palestine.

title: First Ottoman regiment enters Mount Lebanon via Zahle
why: Ottoman troops occupied the mutasarrifate, in effect turning it into a vilayet; first regiment reached Dhour al-Shwer in a snowstorm.

title: Jamal Pasha proclaims martial law over Mount Lebanon
why: Statement from Damascus told Mount Lebanon to accept martial law, stay loyal and calm; mutasarrif Ohannes became subordinate to him.

title: Ottomans abolish Mount Lebanon's semi-autonomous status (other sources: 1915)
why: Sources differ: some date it to the war's start, others place the legal annulment on 11 July 1915 after Ohannes resigned.

title: Jamal Pasha's first expedition against the Suez Canal fails
why: Failed attack (3 Feb 1915 in one source) fed the blockade, requisitioning and repression that fell on Lebanon. (corrected from 1915-01: expedition against Egypt chronology gives 2-3 February 1915)

title: Jamal Pasha cordons off Mount Lebanon; Allied blockade of the coast
why: Allied ships blockaded the Eastern Mediterranean while Jamal barred Bekaa and Syrian grain from the mountain; both combined into famine. (date corrected from 1915-02 to 1915: Allied blockade formally declared 25 Aug 1915; Jamal barred Syrian grain from the mountain)

title: Father Youssef Hayek arrested for writing to a French official
why: Accused of corresponding with Paul Deschanel; hanged on 6 May 1916 as a message that Entente contact meant execution.

title: Constantinople Agreement: France and Britain accept Russian claim on the Straits
why: In the same weeks France staked its claim to annex Syria (including Lebanon) and Cilicia, a root of the later mandate.

title: Locust swarms strike Mount Lebanon and Greater Syria for about three months
why: After a drought-hit harvest, locusts devoured the remaining crops, a main natural trigger of the famine.

title: Provisional law gives Jamal Pasha emergency powers over Syria
why: All Istanbul decrees concerning Syria became subject to his approval, the legal basis for martial rule in Lebanon.

title: Ohannes Pasha resigns as mutasarrif under pressure from Jamal Pasha
why: He refused to renew the Administrative Council with Jamal-approved appointees; resignation was first ignored, then accepted.

title: Ottoman government formally annuls the mutasarrifate protocols
why: The Interior Ministry then appointed Turkish, non-Christian administrators, ending Mount Lebanon's autonomy (one source's date).

title: Decree appoints Ali Munif Bey administrator of Mount Lebanon
why: Date from one Turkish thesis chronology; he arrived in Beirut on 20 September 1915 and began dismantling the old system.

title: 11 Arab nationalists hanged in Beirut after Aley and Damascus trials
why: First group of Arabists executed; one source says 58 sentenced to death, 45 absent, 2 reprieved, 10 Muslims and 1 Christian hanged.

title: Jamal Pasha sets up military court at Aley
why: The summary tribunal in Aley tried people for disloyalty and confiscated property of enemy nationals; sentences were carried out in Beirut and Damascus.

title: French warships evacuate Armenians from Musa Dagh to Port Said
why: About 4,000 people were rescued; many later resettled in Anjar, Lebanon (1939). Counts vary 3,004-4,231 across sources.

title: Ali Munif Bey reaches Beirut and starts dismantling Mount Lebanon's system
why: Reorganised districts and brought in outside officials; later appointed Shehab, Arslan and al-Rami to the Ottoman parliament.

title: Maronite Patriarch Hoayek shelters Armenian refugees despite the famine
why: Wikipedia quotes him: 'The piece of bread that we have, we will share it with our Armenian brothers.'

title: Ottomans end Maronite clerical privileges; Hoayek threatened with exile
why: Jamal forced the patriarchate to seek a sultanic firman for patriarchal appointments; Bishop Boutros Shebli exiled to Adana, where he died.

title: Beirut mayor Ahmad Mukhtar Beyhum deposed by the governor; Umar Daouk appointed mayor
why: Mayor Ahmad Mukhtar Beyhum was dismissed as a potential agitator; the Ottoman governor Azmi Bey installed Daouk. (title corrected: source says Beyhum was deposed by the governor and Daouk appointed in 1915; it does not mention a Jamal-appointed committee)

title: McMahon-Hussein correspondence begins (July 1915 to March 1916)
why: British pledges of Arab independence, later read by Arabs as covering Lebanon, collided with the Sykes-Picot partition.

title: Allied expulsions and Ottoman closures gut foreign missions and services
why: British, French and Russian nationals and missionaries were expelled from Beirut and Mount Lebanon; many schools and clinics closed.

title: Jamal Pasha closes newspapers and dissolves associations in Lebanon
why: Also imposed forced labour, spies and transport disruption; Lebanese treated as suspect subjects.

title: Disease follows hunger: typhus, malaria and lice spread
why: Malnourished civilians and troop movements spread epidemics; disease was a leading killer alongside starvation.

title: Great Famine of Mount Lebanon begins, known as Kafno
why: Mass starvation through 1918 under blockade, requisitioning and crop failure; Wikipedia estimates about 200,000 dead of about 400,000 inhabitants.

title: Black market in grain runs on strategic withholding and usury
why: Merchants withheld grain for weeks to raise prices; Beirut municipality tried but failed to curb it.

title: Jamal reportedly makes secret peace feelers with the Allies (end 1915)
why: Reportedly proposed ruling Syria as king; nothing came of it. Treat as unverified wartime story.

title: Sykes and Picot initial memorandum partitioning Ottoman Arab lands
why: Allots Syria and Lebanon to French control; ratified 9 and 16 May 1916; later basis of the 1918 Modus Vivendi and the mandate.

title: Allied-blockade famine at peak; Gibran writes 80,000 already dead
why: Letter of 26 May 1916 to Mary Haskell blames Ottoman policy; a contemporary claim, not a verified count.

title: Jamal Pasha hangs 14 nationalists in Beirut's Burj Square
why: Martyrs' Day: 21 executed that day (14 Beirut, 7 Damascus); Beirut's square became Martyrs' Square.

title: Seven nationalists hanged in Marjeh Square, Damascus (Martyrs' Day)
why: Same day as Beirut; victims included Shukri al-Asali, Abdelhamid al-Zahrawi and Shafiq al-Muayyad al-Azm.

title: Beirut victims included Father Joseph Hayek and the El Khazen brothers
why: Also hanged: Emir Aref Chehab, Abdel Wahab al-Inglizi and Muhammad Mahmassani; journalists Philippe and Farid El Khazen were from Jounieh.

title: Jamal Pasha's 1915-16 executions of Syrian and Lebanese politicians total 34
why: Wikipedia's Jamal page says 34 executed between 1915 and 1916; other sources give 11 plus 21 (32).

title: About 2,000 Arabist families exiled to Anatolia
why: Alongside the hangings; policy aimed at making Syria more amenable to direct state control. (date approximate: source gives no month for the exile)

title: US Syrian-Mount Lebanon Relief Committee formed (Najib Maalouf chair)
why: Diaspora relief in the United States; Ameen Rihani was assistant chair.

title: Sharif Hussein proclaims the Arab Revolt in Mecca
why: Started against the Ottomans (Jamal's Fourth Army also under pressure); heightened Jamal's suspicion of Syrian Arabs.

title: US collier Caesar leaves with $250,000 relief for Mount Lebanon
why: The 'Christmas Ship' carried flour, wheat, sugar and medicine; Jamal demanded to control distribution and it never reached Lebanon.

title: Mount Lebanon under Ottoman martial rule, forced labour and requisitions
why: Beasts of burden and grain requisitioned for Jamal's campaigns; transport animals shortage blocked famine aid.

title: Soup kitchens set up with little effect on starvation
why: Kitchens run by SPC-affiliated staff, incl. Abeih and Souk el Gharb; Dr Arthur Dray's Brummana model fed about 1,500 people a day; could not match need. (corrected from 1916: AUB exhibit places them in 1915)

title: Lebanese in Egypt fund food shipments via Arwad to the Maronite patriarchate
why: Convents distributed relief to the population; Hoayek received funds from the diaspora and France.

title: American Red Cross barred from direct aid in Mount Lebanon
why: Coincided with the Caesar failure and worsening German-US relations; ended the last wartime Red Cross effort in Syria.

title: Ali Munif becomes Beirut governor; Ismail Haqqi mutasarrif of Mount Lebanon
why: Third Turkish administrator; Haqqi wrote a report on Lebanon's wartime misery.

title: Syrian Central Committee founded in Paris
why: Lebanese-Syrian expatriate network later led by Chekri Ghanem, lobbying for French-guided Syria at the peace conference.

title: Bolsheviks publish the Sykes-Picot terms
why: Revealing the partition embarrassed Britain and dismayed the Arabs; Jamal tried reconciling with Sharif Hussein.

title: Jamal Pasha leaves Syria for Istanbul for good
why: He took leave as Jerusalem fell (9 Dec 1917) and never returned; his rule over Lebanon ended.

title: Flour reaches 250-300 piastres per ratl in spring 1918
why: Against 2-4 piastres before the war, per Near East Relief; a week's food per person cost 7-9 liras.

title: Mount Lebanon population estimated at about 200,000 in 1918
why: Down from 414,747 in 1913 per Wikipedia's infobox, reflecting famine, disease and emigration.

title: Famine death-toll estimates for Mount Lebanon range 100,000 to 300,000
why: Sources: 100,000-200,000 (The National), 150,000-300,000 (Tanielian), 200,000 (Wikipedia), 250,000 (American Red Cross). No reliable census.

title: Greater Syria famine toll estimated 350,000 (Antonius) to 500,000 (Schilcher)
why: Schilcher's higher figure rests on German records; Beirut is said to have lost about half its residents.

title: Famine kills about one-third of Greater Syria's population by Oct 1918 (Tanielian)
why: Hunger and disease, as Beirut city, closed to imports, filled with destitute refugees.

title: Beirut mayor Umar Daouk receives telegram urging a free Arab government
why: From Emir Said al-Jazairi of Damascus; notables met that night at Salim Ali Salam's house to avoid fighting.

title: Ottoman governor leaves Beirut; Arab government proclaimed under Umar Daouk
why: Multi-confessional administration proclaimed; Mumtaz Bey also handed Mount Lebanon to Habib Fayyad before leaving Baabda.

title: Allied and Arab forces enter Damascus; Ottoman rule collapses in Syria
why: Triggers Ottoman withdrawal from Lebanon; Damascus, Beirut and Baabda fell in effect within days.

title: Arab flag formally raised over Beirut Grand Serail
why: Ceremony attended by Faisal's representative Gen. Shukri al-Ayyubi (other sources: he arrived in Beirut on 7 October).

title: First British armoured cars reach Beirut; French ships in harbour
why: Ottoman forces had already left and an Arab government under Shukri al-Ayyubi was in place.

title: Allied cavalry occupy Beirut, 600 Ottoman prisoners taken
why: XXI Corps cavalry entered; French troops also landed (7th Meerut division followed); about 660 Ottoman soldiers surrendered.
actors: Détachement Français de Palestine et de Syrie

title: Arab flag lowered in Beirut; Col. Piépape military governor
why: Allenby ordered removal of Arab governments after French protest; Bulfin appointed Philpin de Piépape governor.

title: British advance to Tripoli; Baalbek taken with 500 Ottoman surrenders
why: Press report of the Allied northward drive after French naval ships left Tripoli's port on 10 October. (corrected from 1918-10-11: Allenby dispatch says armoured cars occupied Baalbek on 9 October taking over 500 Turks; Tripoli occupied 13 October)

title: French infantry detachment reaches Beirut
why: Garrisoning Beirut, Sidon and Tyre; French cavalry followed on 24 October and the 54th Division on 31 October.

title: Allenby proclaims OETA: West zone for Lebanon under French administrator
why: Piépape chief administrator of North/West; OETA West covered Beirut vilayet, Mount Lebanon and Latakia sanjak.

title: Gen. Jules Hamelin replaces Piépape as OETA West administrator
why: Served until 21 November 1919; Habib Pasha Saad's council continued in Baabda as local authority.

title: OETA North renamed OETA West; Cilicia becomes new OETA North
why: Following the occupation of the Adana Vilayet in December 1918.

title: Mount Lebanon Administrative Council meets and drafts Paris demands
why: Sought independence within natural boundaries under French tutelage; sent five-man delegation led by Daoud Ammoun.

title: Paris Peace Conference opens
why: Venue where Lebanese, Syrian and Arab delegations competed to define the post-Ottoman Levant.

title: Daoud Ammoun presents Lebanon's case to the Council of Ten
why: Delegation of the Administrative Council with Druze and Muslim delegates asked for independence, historic borders and French collaboration.

title: Chekri Ghanem and Faisal address the Council of Ten for Syria
why: Ghanem sought separate states under French mandate incl. Greater Lebanon; Faisal said Lebanon belonged to the promised Arab kingdom.

title: Administrative Council declares Lebanon's independence within its borders
why: Vague declaration of 'political and administrative independence'; Hoayek mobilised towns, with cedar flags beside French flags.

title: King-Crane Commission leaves Paris for the Levant
why: American-only inquiry after Britain and France withdrew, to gauge local opinion on mandates.

title: Syrian Congress holds first session under Hashim al-Atassi
why: Nationalist body that backed United Syria incl. Lebanon; opposed French claims and Greater Lebanon.

title: King-Crane Commission arrives in Jaffa; 42-day tour begins
why: Tour of Palestine, Syria, Lebanon and Cilicia until 21 July 1919, collecting 1,863 petitions with 91,079 signatures.

title: Administrative Council names Patriarch Hoayek head of second delegation
why: He would present Lebanese demands in Paris and, days earlier, the King-Crane Commission.

title: Syrian Congress resolves for independent Syria under Faisal, refuses French claims
why: Wanted US help; the resolutions rejected a separate Lebanon in the Syrian framework.

title: King-Crane Commission reaches Lebanon: Baalbek to Beirut
why: Interviews in Beirut 7-8 July, Jbeil, Batroun and Bkerke 9 July, Sidon and Tyre 10 July.

title: King-Crane Commission hears Aaynab, Baabda and Zahle; Tripoli on 12 July
why: Ten days in OETA West; heard delegations from every part of French-administered Lebanon.

title: Patriarch Hoayek leaves for Paris via Jounieh with six-member delegation
why: French required departure from Jounieh, not Beirut, to avoid friction with Faisal's supporters.

title: King-Crane report submitted; Lebanon petitions split on Greater Lebanon
why: Of 446 petitions from OETA West, 196 backed independent Greater Lebanon and 108 opposed; across Syria 80.4% wanted United Syria.

title: French President Poincaré receives Hoayek delegation at the Élysée
why: Part of the Maronite campaign for a larger Lebanon under French protection.

title: Lloyd George and Clemenceau agree British withdrawal, French garrison of Lebanon
why: Aide-mémoire dated 13 Sept; Belleten says 5 Sept. British troops replaced by French west of Sykes-Picot line from 1 Nov 1919.

title: 400 Musa Dagh Armenians return via Beirut quarantine and refugee camp
why: Aboard French warship Diderot from Port Said; they left on 6 October for Alexandretta.

title: Hoayek presents memorandum to the Peace Conference (dated 25 Oct)
why: Les Revendications du Liban: extend Lebanon to Beirut, Tripoli, Sidon, Tyre, Bekaa and Akkar, with independence and French protection.

title: British begin evacuating Syria; French troops take over Lebanese coast and Bekaa
why: Garrisons west of Sykes-Picot line passed to French; Damascus, Homs, Hama, Aleppo to Faisal's Arab force.

title: Clemenceau receives Hoayek; letter of 10 November gives no firm pledge
why: The French response avoided a clear commitment to Greater Lebanon's borders.

title: François Georges Barb takes over OETA West from Hamelin
why: Last OETA West administrator (until 1 Sept 1920).

title: General Gouraud named high commissioner; British leave Damascus
why: Gouraud arrived Beirut in Nov 1919 as commander of the Army of the Levant, with Robert de Caix as political chief.

title: Administrative Council adopts a resolution on Lebanon's status
why: Text appears as Appendix C to Zamir's study; content not read, so treat as a pointer.

title: OETA West population estimate: 1,095,000 (King-Crane table)
why: About 600,000 Muslims, 400,000 Christians, 60,000 Druze, 15,000 Jews; a rough 1919 demographic baseline.

title: Near East Relief shelters house about 45,000 Syrian orphans after the war
why: Orphanages included Zahle, Tripoli, Deir al-Qamar, Ghazir, Sidon, Antelias and Jbeil.

title: Faisal-Clemenceau accord: France recognises Faisal; Lebanon in French zone
why: Secret deal, disavowed by Faisal's nationalist base; prompted a third Lebanese delegation to Paris under Bishop Abdallah al-Khoury.

title: Syrian Congress proclaims Faisal king of Syria including Lebanon
why: Repudiated by Britain and France; spurred Baabda's 22 March independence declaration (already in index) and San Remo.

title: Seven of eleven Administrative Council members seek accord with Faisal
why: They proposed joint Syria-Lebanon independence; French arrested them en route to Damascus. (corrected from 1920-07-10: Rogan dates the memorandum to July 1920; 10 July is when Gouraud reported the arrests)

title: Gouraud ultimatum to Faisal: submit or abdicate
why: Faisal accepted but War Minister Yusuf al-Azma marched to Maysalun (24 July, already in index).

title: Lebanese Maronites reportedly celebrate Maysalun, some fought with French
why: Salibi: volunteers reportedly joined the French; the celebration was remembered in Damascus.

title: Arab Kingdom of Syria abolished; French rule installed in Damascus
why: Pro-French Syrian government declared the day after French entered Damascus.

title: Gouraud proclaims Bekaa's incorporation at Zahle's Grand Kadri Hotel
why: Millerand wrote Archbishop Khoury that Bekaa claims were granted (index has Arrêté 299 on 3 Aug).

title: OETA West administration ends as State of Greater Lebanon begins
why: Administrator Barb's term ended 1 Sept 1920 as Gouraud proclaimed Greater Lebanon.
